questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: International focus, learning German and the prices

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Highly recommended

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University is helpful and you can contact them with problems, the city administration is difficult if you don't speak German, so I recommend getting a German-speaker if you don't

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a buddy who could help me and I got the contact info of the person responsible for international law students - these two helped with everything I needed. There were introductionary lectures as well, but they proved somewhat redundant, as the info was easily available online

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The studentwerk (housing through the university) is cheap and mid-to-low quality, whilst the private market is more expensive but better quality. I recommend the studentwerk, as you'll live together with other international students and have plenty of opportunities to be social.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is public transportation to everything in Mannheim from all the student dorms, either bus, tram or both, and you can buy a semester-ticket for 180 euro which allows you to use all public transport in the Mannheim-Heidelberg area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing is cheap and therefore old. It is charming in it's own weird way, but you'll have friends nearby which, for exchange, is very good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Registering with the university is easy, as there is almost no registration process beyond ordering a student-ID and registering for classes (both easy things). Registering with the city is difficult and should be done in-person with a German-speaker at hand (unless you speak it yourself)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You write an email asking for classes and then later you write an email asking for a student-ID. Very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was not necessary, however they did offer (badly) translated versions of the forms relevant when dealing with the city.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a German-speaker when dealing with non-university important stuff (such as getting a German number or dealing with the city at all).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors were great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I got MA-programmes as well, and they were not too difficult. Don't be scared by the 1-hour exams, as they are pretty simple questions (a la RJM) and the oral exams are also easier. There is not the same solemnity in German exams as in Danish exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The material was exclusively covered by the professors, so (almost) no student presentations, but participation was encouraged and sometimes graded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European Private Law
Comparative Law I: European Legal Traditions
German Constitutional Law
International Arbitration
EU Fundamental Rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Comparative Law, for the professor (prof. Brandt) who is really great. 
EU Fundamental Rights, if you don't mind a competent, but intense professor
International Arbitration, as it gives you an understanding for basic arbitration and is a really good introduction into the arbitrational world.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Germany is, comparatively, cheap and thus I eat out and went out more than at home. You could easily live for less then I did. There aren't many "unexpected" costs beyond a semester fee of about 100 euros.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything seemed cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They tried their best, but most things were limited because of corona.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports had their own department and beyond that there were many clubs avaliable. They can be found on the website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not personally perticipate in many activities, but the gym membership is free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Heidelberg - it's beautiful and historic and free with the semester ticket. Beyond that there are wine-fields, small towns and France nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: German culture is close to Danish, so adjusting is easy. As regards the other international students, I recommend taking what they say at face value, what you might think is sarcasm or a joke, might very well not be - and try to keep an open mind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with other internationals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Smoking indoors is not prohibited - incredibly frustrating.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, as I love German food - especially at the Christmas Market

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do the summer academy if possible, it is kinda pricey, but you'll meet a lot of people and get a solid foundation in German which is really helpful.
If you drink, then go to Jungbusch.
Enjoy your time - five months are not that long.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember the exchange rate - things might not be as cheap as they appear.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people from across the world and thus understanding the world a little bit better.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Germany is, unlike Denmark, a very analogue country, so if there is an option to do things online, it's usually incredibly bad.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I can strongly recommend going - Mannheim is absolutely a great place to study abroad. Should you have any questions, please contact me on zmb695@

questions.answer: Yes
